security_audit.summary: I found no executable malicious behavior in the reviewed skill. The static command, reconnaissance, sensitive-file, and environment findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and Go sample code. The skill is documentation-only, but examples should be labeled clearly to reduce scanner noise.

remediation.suggestion: Clarify that configuration values are read locally and must never be logged or transmitted.

content.value_statement: Large Go systems can lose clear boundaries as teams add features. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured patterns for clean architecture, DDD, and production service layout.
actual_capabilities: Explains clean architecture package layout for Go services.
Shows domain repository, service, and port interface examples.
Demonstrates SQL persistence adapter patterns with dependency inversion.
Covers aggregate roots, value objects, and domain events.
Describes manual and Wire-style dependency injection.
Provides configuration and custom error handling examples.
limitations: Provides guidance and snippets, not a runnable code generator.
Examples omit full imports, tests, migrations, and security hardening.
Does not cover every framework, cloud provider, or database driver.
Requires user review before applying patterns to production systems.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Go Service
use_cases.description: Define package boundaries, dependency direction, and service layers before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Architecture
use_cases.description: Create shared patterns for repositories, services, ports, adapters, and application wiring.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Growing Codebase
use_cases.description: Move business rules into domain and application layers while keeping infrastructure isolated.

prompt_templates.title: Map a New Service
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new Go API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the golang-enterprise-patterns skill to propose a clean architecture layout for a new Go API. Include packages, dependency direction, and boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Define Ports and Adapters
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design ports and adapters for a Go service with database storage and notifications. Explain each interface and adapter responsibility.

prompt_templates.title: Model a Domain Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced DDD modeling for business logic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to model an order workflow with aggregates, value objects, domain events, and invariants. Keep infrastructure outside the domain.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Boundaries
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing Go service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a Go service for clean architecture violations. Identify misplaced dependencies, unclear boundaries, and concrete refactoring steps.

output_examples.input: A team wants to split a monolithic Go API into clearer layers.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a package map with domain, application, infrastructure, and interface layers. It explains which dependencies point inward.

output_examples.input: A service needs database storage and welcome email delivery.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies primary and secondary ports, then assigns database and notification adapters to infrastructure packages.

output_examples.input: An order workflow needs stronger business rules.
output_examples.output: The assistant describes an aggregate root, value objects, domain events, and validation rules that protect order state changes.

best_practices: Start with domain rules and use cases before choosing infrastructure details.
Keep interfaces small and define them near the layer that owns the behavior.
Use explicit constructors and configuration boundaries for production services.
anti_patterns: Do not let database models become the domain model by default.
Do not place business rules inside HTTP handlers or persistence adapters.
Do not add architecture layers that have no clear responsibility.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps design enterprise Go services with clean architecture, hexagonal architecture, DDD, dependency injection, configuration, and error handling patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance and example snippets that users adapt to their own codebase.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for architecture planning and code review prompts.

faq.question: Is it limited to one Go framework?
faq.answer: No. The patterns focus on package boundaries and dependencies, so they can fit many Go frameworks.

faq.question: Does it include database guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows repository and persistence adapter patterns, including parameterized SQL examples.

faq.question: What should users review before production use?
faq.answer: Users should add tests, imports, migrations, observability, security controls, and framework-specific details before shipping.
